27th March 191 6
REPORT ON a seizure of arms at Pootung.
（批：Kro 29/3/16）
Made by D.S.I. Brewster Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.

Sir
In view of the seizure of ammunition in Gordon Road District
the details of another seizure which occured in 1903 may be of
interest.
About the end of February 1903 the Customs Authorities with
the assistance of the Chinese Police, seized a large quantity of
ammunition which was in a warehouse situated near Lan Ni Deu
Pootung opposite the French Bund and leased by Messrs H.M.Schultz
and Co and Telge and Schroeter. At the timeof the seizure it
appears that a Rebellion on a small scale was brewing in the Kwan-
gsi Provence, hence the activity of the Chinese Authorities. As
a result of the seizure and the consequent investigations, the
following letter from the German Consul General, preceeded by
Editorial comment, was published in the North China Daily News of
the 6th March 1903.
Various statements have been current with reference with ref-
erence to a large quantity of arms and ammunition recently found
at Pootung, and in justice to Messrs Telge and Schroeter we publish
the following letter:-
Imperial German Consulate General,
Shanghai, 5th March 1903.b
Dear Sir
On behalf of Messrs Telge and Schroeter I have the honour
to give you the following particulars about the cases of ammunition
stored in the Chintung godown at Pootung:-
T.T.1/95- 95 cases Mauser cartridges, 200,000.ex Lysemoon Alesia.
3.2.1900.
（批：Seen by C.I.A. 28/3/16 -）

先生：
鉴于在戈登路地区查获弹药一事，1903年发生的另一起查获案件的细节或许令人感兴趣。
1903年2月底，海关当局在中国警方的协助下，查获了大量弹药，这些弹药存放在位于浦东兰尼渡（Lan Ni Deu，音译）附近、法外滩对面的一处仓库内，该仓库由 H.M. Schultz 公司以及 Telge 和 Schroeter 公司租赁。在查获当时，广西省似乎正酝酿着一场小规模的反叛，因此中国当局采取了行动。作为此次查获及随后调查的结果，1903年3月6日的《字林西报》刊登了以下来自德国总领事的信件，并附有编者按：
关于最近在浦东发现的大量武器和弹药，流传着各种说法。为了公正对待 Telge 和 Schroeter 先生，我们刊登以下信件：-
德意志帝国驻上海总领事馆，
1903年3月5日。
亲爱的先生：
谨代表 Telge 和 Schroeter 先生，荣幸地向您提供有关存放在浦东金通（Chintung，音译）栈房的弹药箱的详情：-
T.T.1/95- 95箱毛瑟枪子弹，共200,000发，源自“Lysemoon Alesia”号轮船。
1900年2月3日。
（批注：刑事侦缉处处长阅 1916年3月28日 -）

All this cargo arriving when troubles were threatening in the
North, Messrs Telge and Schroeter had to store the ammunition
in Shanghai by order of this Consulate. The 1,000 rifles
and 500,000 cartridges were transferred to H.E. Chang Chih-tang
later on and transhipped to Hankow per s.s. "Suitai" the 7th
July 1900 under special permission of this Consulate, whilst the
5,000 rifles and 1,500,000 rounds of ammunition were still
kept here. Owing to the dangerous nature of cartridges and
the prohibition of storing them within the limits of the Settlement
Telge

Sir
I have examined the boxes containing the ammunition referred
to above,with a view to ascertaining whether the marks on the
boxes corresponded with those referred to in the letter from the
German Consul General which I forwarded yesterday.
The marks do not correspond. Only one of the shell
boxes is marked W.K.& Co while the other ammunition boxes are
marked Q.R. or X.Z. with numbers.
Your Obedient Servant
M Brewster

Sir
I respectfully beg to report that I have been to
the Customs to try to find out if the ammunition in
question passed through the customs in the usual way.
I saw the Deputy Commissioner who informed me that
it is against their regulations to give any information
of this nature, and suggested that the Captain
Superintendent write to the Commissioner for the
desired information.
Attached is a list of the markings on the various
cases.
One of the armour piercing shells has been opened and
the words "Hotchkiss Paris" is written on the inside.

I beg to remain
Sir

J. Sullivan. D. S. 36.

REPORT ON the seizure of ammunition at Gordon Road Station.
Made by D.S.I. Brewster Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir
This afternoon I accompanied a Representative of the French
Police and Neilson,s Chauffeur, who is still in custody in French-
town, to Gordon Road Station in order to give the Chauffeur an
opportunity of identifying the boxes of ammunition there. He
stated that he had never seen long boxes similar to those containing
the shells but he had carried in the car to his masters house on
Siccawei Road, several boxes somewhat similar to that containing
the pistol ammunition. He also stated that he had often driven
past, but never stopped at No 1 Yu Yuen Road.
Your Obedient Servant
MB Brewster.
D.S.I.
Chief Det Insp.

Translation of an extract from Deutsche Zeitung
fur China dated 10th April 1916.

Don Quixote.

Very seldom has there been a case in the Mixed Court
with so many suggestions. Very seldom had the M.C.
through ignorance, falsehood and wickedness produced
so many suggestions as the article in the North China
Daily News from Saturday morning the 8th April shows.
It is entitled "German plots in Shanghai".
Perhaps there is a lot of Salomonic wisdom in the
heads of the English Assessor Grant Jones and the
Police Legal Adviser Newman. Yes they are heroes,
heroes who have served their country.
The forgery of a permit which nobody has seen
and Newman's ghost ship the Delcke Rickmers.
Sommers and Nielsen whom they do not even know
by sight are accomplices.
The Chief of Police a man without manners in his
behaviour against Mr. Sommers which was denied with
impudence. The Chinese authorities who are bad
conspirators and Nielsen who never dined at the
German Consulate is called the "Weekly
Tiffin guest".
A proper political case, similar to that in the
French Mixed Court. Would that not be a glorious
victory if they deported the German Consulate or do
they think that with the deportation of the German
Consulate, the Germans would be finished in China?
Are we guests here? No. We have the same rights
as the English, Americans, Swedes, Danes or Norwegians.
Woe, woe to the scoundrels, who are trying to
take our rights and want to drive us from
House and Home.

1916年4月10日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）摘录译文。

堂吉诃德。

混合法庭上很少出现有如此多暗示的案件。混合法庭也很少因无知、虚假和邪恶而产生如此多的暗示，正如4月8日星期六上午《字林西报》上的文章所示。
该文章题为“上海德国的阴谋”。
也许英国陪审员格兰特·琼斯（Grant Jones）和警务法律顾问纽曼（Newman）的头脑中有很多所罗门式的智慧。是的，他们是英雄，是为国家服务的英雄。
伪造了一份无人见过的许可证，还有纽曼的幽灵船“Delcke Rickmers”号。
他们甚至没见过面的 Sommers 和 Nielsen 成了同谋。
警察局长是一个没有礼貌的人，他对 Sommers 先生的行为粗鲁无礼，却厚颜无耻地予以否认。中国当局是糟糕的阴谋家，而从未在德国领事馆用餐的 Nielsen 被称为“每周午餐常客”。
一个真正的政治案件，类似于法租界混合法庭的案件。如果他们驱逐德国领事馆，那难道不是一场光荣的胜利吗？还是他们认为，一旦驱逐了德国领事馆，德国人在中国就完蛋了？
我们是这里的客人吗？不。我们拥有与英国人、美国人、瑞典人、丹麦人或挪威人相同的权利。
可悲啊，可悲，那些试图剥夺我们的权利、想将我们从家园中赶走的流氓。

Translation of an extract from the Deutsche Zeitung
fur China dated 6th April 1918.

The Arms Case.

The case against the five Chinese who were charged
in the Mixed Court on 25th March for breach of
Municipal Regulations (re transportation of arms
through the International Settlement) was resumed
yesterday.
The Court acquitted the prisoners and the proceedings
show that their arrest and prosecutions was illegal.
As regards the ammunition seized judgement was
reserved until to morrow.
During yesterday's proceedings the Police Legal
Advisor Heaman took the liberty to make statements
against the Deutsche Zeitung fur China which he
called a scurrilous rag.
With due respect to the Court it was its duty
to have put the Police legal adviser back to his proper
place. Anyhow the insult does no harm to us.
It shows merely English spite against everything
German and as the English cannot prove their case
they now seek to raise a wordy warfare. The poor
English they have lost their pride, one defeat
comes after another. They have 1 to 2 Milliards
mark more expenses per month than the Germans and their
old saying about "the free country" is on the rocks.
Naturally the English show their temper against the
Germans anywhere, everywhere and anyhow.
Regarding the statements of a no account Police
Legal Advisor. With reference to our paper already
viewed with displeasure by our enemies we
pass them by as unworthy of notice for as far we are
aware he is unable even to read it.
Referring to the statement "scurrilous rag" this is
as much value as a dog's barking at the moon.
much

1918年4月6日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）摘录译文。

武器案。

3月25日，五名中国人因违反市政条例（关于通过国际租界运输武器）在混合法庭被起诉，该案昨日复审。
法庭宣判被告无罪，诉讼过程显示他们的逮捕和起诉是非法的。关于查获的弹药，判决保留至明日。
在昨日的诉讼过程中，警务法律顾问希曼（Heaman）肆意发表针对《德文新报》的言论，称其为“下流小报”。
出于对法庭的尊重，法庭本有责任让这位警务法律顾问回到他应有的位置。无论如何，这种侮辱对我们并无损害。
这仅仅显示了英国人对一切德国事物的恶意，由于英国人无法证明他们的案件，他们现在试图发动口水战。可怜的英国人，他们失去了骄傲，一次失败接着一次失败。他们每月的开支比德国人多出10到20亿马克，他们关于“自由国度”的老话已陷入困境。
自然，英国人在任何地方、以任何方式对德国人发泄怒气。
关于那位不值一提的警务法律顾问的言论。鉴于我们的报纸已被敌人不满地看待，我们认为这些言论不值得注意，因为据我们所知，他甚至无法阅读它。
至于“下流小报”的说法，其价值如同狗对着月亮吠叫。

page_data.en:
No. 208
Date 29/3/16

The following is a translation of an extract from
the Deutsche Zeitung fur China dated March 27th 1916:-

A new armscase.

The China Press of yesterday made a report in a
rather large advertising style about the seizure
of a quantity of ammunition on the Kerry Road. The
transaction was quite legal as the result of the
Police enquiries show but the China Press connected
this affair in a rather shameless style with the
Nielsen case.
What really happened is this:-
On Saturday morning whilst on patrol a English
policeman of the S.M.P. noticed at the Kerry Road
jetty a boat in charge of a Chinese in naval
uniform. On being questioned by the Policeman
he answered that he was waiting for ammunition
which was to be shipped to the Arsenal.
The Policeman telephoned the facts to the Gordon
Rd Police Station and a Police Inspector arrived.
A few minutes later a cart came along drawn by a
pony followed by five Chinese and by Mr. H. Thomsen
from Shanghai and Mr. Fritz Sommers from Tientsin.
Mr. Sommers had a contract with the Chinese
Government and had the necessary permit with him.
The whole party then proceeded to the Gordon Rd.
Police Station at the request of the Police
Inspector where the Chinese and the ammunition
were detained. All the protest of the German gentlemen
were of no avail. Mr. Sommers, Mr. Thomsen and
the Chinese official then went to see the Chief of the
S.M.P. Mr. Mc Euen who told them that they required
a permit. Mr. Sommers who is a stranger in Shanghai
obtained a permit from the German Consulate which
was also signed by the Senior Consul (The Belgian
Consul General Siffert) but still the Police refused
to release the Chinese and the ammunition.
The Chinese were taken to the Mixed Court this
morning before the English Assessor Mrant Jones
and at the request of the Police the case was
remanded till Friday.
Mr. Muaso appeared for the Chinese Government.
After the loud advertising of the China Press a
suprisingly tame article was published by the
North China Daily News.
The arrest of the five Chinese and the seizure
of the ammunition by the Police is illegal it is
against the Bye Law 827 of the Land Regulations which
says that permit is not required whilst shipping
arms and ammunition through the International Settlement
if in charge of a responsible official in this case
the transport was accompanied by a Chinese naval officer.

第208号
日期 1916年3月29日

以下是1916年3月27日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）摘录的译文：

一起新的军火案。

昨日的《字林西报》（The China Press）以类似大幅广告的风格报道了在嘉里路（Kerry Road）查获一批弹药的事件。警务处的调查结果显示，该交易完全合法，但《字林西报》却以一种相当无耻的方式将此事件与尼尔森案（Nielsen case）联系起来。
事实真相如下：
周六上午，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的一名英国巡警在嘉里路码头注意到一艘由一名身穿海军制服的中国人负责的船只。当巡警询问时，他回答说正在等待要运往兵工厂的弹药。
巡警将情况电话报告给戈登路（Gordon Rd.）捕房，随后一名巡官抵达。几分钟后，一辆由小马驹拉着的马车驶来，后面跟着五名中国人，以及来自上海的H.汤姆森先生（Mr. H. Thomsen）和来自天津的弗里茨·索默斯先生（Mr. Fritz Sommers）。索默斯先生与中国政府签有合同，并随身携带了必要的许可证。应巡官要求，全体人员随后前往戈登路捕房，那里的中国人和弹药被扣留。几位德国绅士的所有抗议均无济于事。随后，索默斯先生、汤姆森先生和那位中国官员去见上海公共租界工部局警务处处长麦基恩先生（Mr. Mc Euen），麦基恩先生告诉他们需要许可证。作为上海陌生人的索默斯先生从德国领事馆获得了一份许可证，该许可证也由资深领事（比利时总领事西费尔特 Siffert）签署，但警方仍拒绝释放那名中国人和弹药。
今天上午，这些中国人被带至混合法庭，在英国陪审判员琼斯先生（Mrant Jones，原文如此，应为Grant Jones或类似名字，此处依原文音译或保留疑点，但根据后文确认为Grant Jones，此处暂按原文拼写处理或修正为通用译名，鉴于后文出现Grant Jones，此处Mrant极可能是OCR错误，但按要求不脑补，故保留原文拼写对应的音译或标注）面前受审，应警方请求，案件延期至周五审理。
穆阿索先生（Mr. Muaso，音译）代表中国政府出庭。
在《字林西报》大肆宣扬之后，《字林报》（North China Daily News）刊登了一篇出人意料地温和的文章。
警方逮捕五名中国人并扣押弹药是非法的，这违反了《土地章程》附律第827条，该条规定，如果由负责任的中国官员负责，在国际租界内运输武器和弹药无需许可证；在本案中，运输过程有一名中国海军军官陪同。

I. O. R&C
Date 6/4/16
No 203

Translation of an extract from the Deutsche Zeitung
fur China dated 1st April 1916.

Two Political proceedings.
The last arms transactions.

At the Mixed Court proceedings were again continued
against the five Chinese charged with transporting
ammunition through the Settlement.
The proceedings were purely political it does not
matter to the Court what becomes of the Chinese
as the English authorities only want to score points
against the German Government.
The statement about the breach of the Land Regulations
37 is untrue as the cargo was accompanied by a naval
officer in uniform according to the rules.
The Police of the International Settlement is working
hard to connect this affair with the alleged German
plots as the evidence of a British employee of
the Kiangnan wharf, R.H.Mauchan, shows. The evidence
was given in such a way that the public should
think that the s.s. Deike Rickmers had shifted
her berth for the sole purpose of getting
the four guns on board and to disappear quickly
from the river and to appear somewhere suddenly
as an armed cruiser.
Admiral Wong was made to look like a traitor who
works hand in hand with the German Government.
Had Mr. Mauchan the right to give the
secrets of the Chinese Government away in a open Court?
The best part of the proceedings was the evidence of
Mr. Sommer and he made the Police look small.
The Court wanted to know the whereabouts of four
guns as a letter from the Commissioner of the
Customs produced in Court showed no records
but Mr. Sommers soon straightened the matter
in going back to the year 1900 and mentioning the
name of the s.s. Holstatia. The Commissioner of
Customs appeared not to know his own books.
It was a surprise to the Court. But what
about the question where are the four guns?
If the Chief of the Police Mr. Mc Euen had attended
to his business properly instead of running to the
Kiangwan races, and betting on ponies he would be
a wiser man now. Then the permit issued by the
German Consulate and signed by the Senior Consul which
was produced to him By Mr. Sommers had the number
of the godown and the name of the street where the
four guns were but now after the treatment Mr.
Sommers received from the Police it is up to them to
find it out.
It is well that a man not connected with Shanghai
told the truth about the International Police.
The Police is purely a British Concern who take
its instructions only from the English authorities.
But all the rubbish in this affair did not
help the unfortunate five Chinese who are still
in custody as the case is remanded till next Wednesday.

I. O. R&C
日期 1916年4月6日
第203号

以下是1916年4月1日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）摘录的译文。

两起政治诉讼。
最近的军火交易。

混合法庭再次继续审理被指控通过租界运输弹药的 five Chinese（五名中国人）的案件。
诉讼纯属政治性质，法庭并不关心这些中国人的命运，因为英国当局只想借此打击德国政府。
关于违反《土地章程》第37条的说法是不实的，因为根据规定，货物由一名身穿制服的海军军官陪同。
国际租界警方正努力将此事件与所谓的德国阴谋联系起来，正如江南码头（Kiangnan wharf）英籍雇员R.H.莫昌（R.H. Mauchan，音译）的证词所示。其作证方式意在让公众认为，“迪克·里克默斯”号轮船（s.s. Deike Rickmers）改变泊位仅仅是为了将四门大炮装上船，然后迅速从河中消失，并突然在某处作为武装巡洋舰出现。
王督军（Admiral Wong，指海军上将或督军王某）被描绘成与德国政府勾结的叛徒。
莫昌先生有权在公开法庭上泄露中国政府的秘密吗？
庭审中最精彩的部分是索默尔先生（Mr. Sommer，即前文Sommers）的证词，他让警方显得渺小无能。
法庭想知道四门大炮的下落，因为当庭出示的海关税务司信函显示没有相关记录，但索默斯先生很快澄清了此事，他追溯到1900年，并提到了“霍尔萨蒂亚”号轮船（s.s. Holstatia）的名字。海关税务司似乎连自己的账册都不清楚。
这让法庭感到惊讶。但是，那四门大炮在哪里的问题呢？
如果警务处处长麦基恩先生（Mr. Mc Euen）妥善履行其职，而不是跑去江湾（Kiangwan）赛马并在小马驹身上下注，他现在会是个更明智的人。当时，索默斯先生向他出示了由德国领事馆签发、并由资深领事签署的许可证，上面写有存放四门大炮的仓库编号和街道名称，但现在，鉴于警方对待索默斯先生的方式，找出大炮下落成了警方的责任。
幸好，一个与上海无关的人说出了关于国际警察的真相。
警方纯粹是英国的机构，只接受英国当局的指令。
但这起事件中所有的胡言乱语并没有帮助那五名不幸的中国人，他们仍被拘留，因为案件已延期至下周三审理。

E. O. SEG
No. 203
Date....................

Translation of an extract from the Deutsche Zeitung
fur China dated April 8th 1916.

A wise and just Judge.

A second Daniel.

We have received particulars about the judgement over the
last arms transaction which finished at the Mixed Court
yesterday.
The English Press calls the judgement a masterpiece but
if everybody thinks so that's a question, it only
shows how the English fear the Germans.
We admit there is a breach of the Bye Law 33 regards
the storing of ammunition at Thompson's house No.1
Yu Yuen Road but don't forget that it is practically
impossible for a German merchant to get a godown
especially from neutrals, thanks to the clever
work of the English.
In the godown where the four guns are, ammunition is
not allowed to be stored, and as the Thompson's house
was suitable it was put there.
The arrest of the five Chinese was illegal but the
Police do not care, it seems to be the practice now
in both Settlements.
The captured ammunition was the property of the Chinese
Government and that's why there was no application for
a German Assessor. The Court thought that $20 for
the hire of a van was unusually high but what about the
Shanghai Horse Bazaar and their charges and there is
another thing, it is very remarkable that the
Police Legal Advisor had forgotten to mention the
presence of a Chinese officer in uniform when the
ammunition was seized. The presence of a Chinese
officer in uniform covers the Bye Law 37. The Police
had no right to open the boxes and have no right to
ask for a permit, there is no such law.
When Mr. Sommers asked the Police Legal Adviser where he
could get a permit, the Police Legal Adviser could not answer.
The permit issued by the German Consulate was only done to
oblige the Chinese Government.
We have from good authority that the English Minister at
Peking had asked the Chinese authorities for information
regards the contracts which are in Germans hands. It shows
the English are after German business again but we wont
quarrel about that.
We are absolutely sure that the English Assessor has made
knowingly a false statement regards the expression of the
Chief of Police Mc Kuen.
The official Chinese Government permit, when it was shown
to Mc Kuen in the presence of Messrs Sommers and Thomsen
and in the presence of the Chinese officer, was returned
with the remark, "No damned use" and he also used the same
expression to the Chinese officer when he produced the
written authority from Admiral Wong.
We don't deny that the figure 35 was added to the originally
figure 44 but it was done by the proper Chinese Authorities
and it is not a forgery, only an economical business transaction.
The reason why Mr. Sommers has not produced the permit in
Court, is because the permit belonged to the Chinese
Government and he had no authority over it.
The Assessor in this case is the same official who heard
the "Medicine for India" case and who called himself at
that time an "official of His Majesty of Great Britain."
To make it short the so-called master piece of judgment
was given under the instructions of higher authority.

10
w.

C. I. D.
E. O. SEG
第203号
日期....................

以下是1916年4月8日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）摘录的译文。

一位明智而公正的法官。

第二个丹尼尔（Daniel，圣经中象征智慧公正的人物）。

我们收到了关于昨天在混合法庭终结的最近一起军火交易案的判决详情。
英国报刊称该判决为杰作，但是否人人都这么想则存疑，这仅显示了英国人对德国人的恐惧。
我们承认在俞园路（Yu Yuen Road）1号汤普森住宅（Thompson's house）储存弹药违反了附律第33条，但不要忘记，由于英国人的巧妙运作，德国商人实际上很难租到仓库，尤其是从中立国人士那里。
存放四门大炮的仓库不允许储存弹药，而汤普森住宅合适，因此弹药被存放在那里。
逮捕五名中国人是非法的，但警方毫不在意，这似乎已成为两个租界目前的惯例。
被查获的弹药是中国政府的财产，因此没有申请德国陪审判员。法庭认为20美元的车费高得离谱，但看看上海马市（Shanghai Horse Bazaar）及其收费标准吧；还有另一件事，非常值得注意的是，警方法律顾问在扣押弹药时忘了提及有一名身穿制服的中国军官在场。身穿制服的中国军官在场这一事实符合附律第37条的规定。警方无权打开箱子，也无权要求出示许可证，因为没有这样的法律。
当索默斯先生询问警方法律顾问在哪里可以获得许可证时，警方法律顾问无法回答。
德国领事馆签发的许可证只是为了满足中国政府的要求而办理的。
我们从可靠渠道获悉，驻北京的英国公使已向中国当局查询有关掌握在德国人手中的合同的信息。这表明英国人又在觊觎德国人的生意，但我们不想就此争论。
我们绝对确信，英国陪审判员故意就警务处处长麦基恩（Mc Kuen，即Mc Euen）的言论作了虚假陈述。
当索默斯先生和汤姆森先生以及那名中国军官在场时，向麦基恩出示的中国政府官方许可证被退回，并附带评论说“毫无该死的用处”（No damned use），当中国军官出示王督军的书面授权时，他也对中国军官使用了同样的措辞。
我们不否认数字35被添加到了原始数字44上，但这是由中国主管当局进行的，并非伪造，只是一项经济性的业务操作。
索默斯先生未在法庭上出示许可证的原因，是因为该许可证属于中国政府，他无权处置。
本案的陪审判员就是审理“印度药品案”的那位官员，他当时自称是“大英陛下政府的官员”。
简而言之，所谓的判决杰作是在上级指示下作出的。

10
w.

203
Translation of an extract from Deutsche Zeitung
für China dated 10th April 1916.

Don Quixote.

Very seldom has there been a case in the Mixed Court
with so many suggestions. Very seldom had the M.C.
through ignorance, falsehood and wickedness produced
so many suggestions as the article in the North China
Daily News from Saturday morning the 8th April shows.
It is entitled "German plots in Shanghai".
Perhaps there is a lot of Salomonic wisdom in the
heads of the English Assessor Grant Jones and the
Police Legal Adviser Newman. Yes they are heroes,
heroes who have served their country.
The forgery of a permit which nobody has seen
and Newman's ghost ship the Dokoku Riokmen.
Sommers and Nielsen when they do not even know
by sight are accomplices.
The Chief of Police a man without manners in his
behaviour against Mr. Sommers which was denied with
impudence. The Chinese authorities who are bad
conspirators and Nielsen who never dined at the
German Consulate is called the "Weekly
Tiffin guest".
A proper political case, similar to that in the
French Mixed Court. Would that not be a glorious
victory if they deported the German Consulate or do
they think that with the deportation of the German
Consulate, the Germans would be finished in China?
Are we guests here? No. We have the same rights
as the English, Americans, Swedes, Danes or Norwegians.
Woe, woe to the scoundrels, who are trying to
take our rights and want to drive us from
House and Home.
page_data.zh:
203
以下是1916年4月10日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung für China）摘录的译文。

堂吉诃德。

混合法庭很少出现有如此多暗示的案件。混合法庭因无知、谎言和邪恶而产生的暗示，很少像4月8日星期六上午《字林报》的文章那样多。该文章题为“上海的德国阴谋”。
也许英国陪审判员格兰特·琼斯（Grant Jones）和警方法律顾问纽曼（Newman）的头脑中充满了所罗门式的智慧。是的，他们是英雄，是为国家服务的英雄。
伪造了一份没人见过的许可证，以及纽曼的幽灵船“Dokoku Riokmen”（音译，原文不清或为特定船名误植）。
索默斯和尼尔森甚至互不相识，却被说成是同谋。
警务处处长是一个举止无礼的人，他对索默斯先生的无礼行为被厚颜无耻地否认。
中国当局被描绘成拙劣的阴谋家，而从未在德国领事馆用餐的尼尔森被称为“每周午餐常客”（Weekly Tiffin guest）。
这是一起典型的政治案件，类似于法国混合法庭的案件。如果他们驱逐德国领事馆，那难道不是一场光荣的胜利吗？还是他们认为驱逐了德国领事馆，德国人在中国的势力就会终结？
我们是这里的客人吗？不。我们拥有与英国人、美国人、瑞典人、丹麦人或挪威人相同的权利。
可悲，可悲啊，那些试图剥夺我们的权利、想将我们赶出家园的流氓们。

page_data.en:
203

Translation of an extract from the Deutsche Zeitung
fur China dated 6th April 1916.

The Arms Case.

The case against the five Chinese who were charged
in the Mixed Court on 25th March for breach of
Municipal Regulations (re transportation of arms
through the International Settlement) was resumed
yesterday.
The Court acquitted the prisoners and the proceedings
show that their arrest and prosecutions was illegal.
As regards the ammunition seized judgement was
reserved until to morrow.
During yesterday's proceedings the Police Legal
Advisor Newman took the liberty to make statements
against the Deutsche Zeitung fur China which he
called a scurrilous rag.
With due regrets to the Court it was its duty
to have put the Police legal adviser back to his proper
place. Anyhow the insult does no harm to us.
It shows merely English spite against everything
German and as the English cannot prove their case
they now seek to raise a wordy warfare. The poor
English they have lost their pride, one defeat
comes after another. They have 1 to 2 Milliards
mark more expenses per month than the Germans and their
old saying about "the free country" is on the rocks.
Naturally the English show their temper against the
Germans anywhere, everywhere and anyhow.
Regarding the statements of a-no-account Police
Legal Adviser. With reference to our paper already
viewed with displeasure by our enemies we
pass them by as unworthy of notice for as far we are
aware he is unable even to read it.
Refering to the statement "scurrilous rag" this is
as much value as a dog's barking at the moon.
hinch

军火案。

针对五名中国人的案件于3月25日在混合法庭因违反市政规章（关于通过国际租界运输武器）而被起诉，昨日恢复审理。
法庭宣判被告无罪，诉讼过程表明对他们的逮捕和起诉是非法的。
关于被扣押弹药的判决保留至明日宣布。
在昨天的诉讼过程中，警方法律顾问纽曼肆意发表针对《德文新报》的言论，称其为“下流的小报”。
出于对法庭的尊重，本有责任让警方法律顾问回到他适当的位置。无论如何，这种侮辱对我们并无损害。
这仅仅显示了英国人对一切德国事物的恶意，由于英国人无法证明其案件成立，他们现在试图发起口水战。可怜的英国人，他们失去了骄傲，一次失败接着一次失败。他们每月的支出比德国人多出10亿至20亿马克，他们关于“自由国度”的老话已陷入困境。
自然，英国人在任何地方、以任何方式向德国人发泄脾气。
关于那位不值一提的警方法律顾问的声明。鉴于我们的报纸已被敌人不满地看待，我们认为这些声明不值得注意，因为据我们所知，他甚至无法阅读我们的报纸。
关于“下流小报”的说法，其价值如同狗对着月亮吠叫。

The following is a translation of an extract from
the Deutsche Zeitung fur China dated March 27th 1916:-

A new armsease.

The China Press of yesterday made a report in a
rather large advertising style about the seizure
of a quantity of ammunition on the Ferry Road. The
transaction was quite legal as the result of the
Police enquiries show but the China Press connected
this affair in a rather shameless style with the
Nielsens case.
What really happened is this:-
On Saturday morning whilst on patrol a English
policemen of the S.M.P. noticed at the Ferry Road
jetty a boat in charge of a Chinese in naval
uniform. On being questioned by the Policeman
he answered that he was waiting for ammunition
which was to be shipped to the Arsenal.
The Policeman telephoned the facts to the Gordon
Rd Police Station and a Police Inspector arrived
A few minutes later a cart came along drawn by a
pony followed by five Chinese and by Mr. H. Thomsen
from Shanghai and Mr. Fritz Sommers from Tientsin.
Mr. Sommers had a contract with the Chinese
Government and had the necessary permit with him.
The whole party then proceeded to the Gordon Rd
Police Station at the request of the Police
Inspector where the Chinese and the ammunition
were detained. All the protest of the German gentlemen
were of no avail. Mr. Sommers , Mr. Thomsen and
the Chinese official then went to see the Chief of the
S.M.P. Mr Mc Euen who told them that they required
a permit. Mr. Sommers who is a stranger in Shanghai
obtained a permit from the German Consulate which
was also signed by the Senior Consul (The Belgian
Consul General Siffert) but still the Police refused
to release the Chinese and the ammunition.
The Chinese were taken to the Mixed Court this
morning before the English Assessor Brant Jones
and at the request of the Police the case was
remanded till Friday.
Mr. Musso appeared for the Chinese Government.
After the loud advertising of the China Press a
suprisingly tame article was published by the
North China Daily News.
The arrest of the five Chinese and the seizure
of the ammunition by the Police is illegal it is
against the Bye Law 87 of the Land Regulations which
says that permit is not required whilst shipping
arms and ammunition through the International Settlement
if in charge of a responsible official in this case
the transport was accompanied by a Chinese naval officer.

以下是1916年3月27日《德文新报》（Deutsche Zeitung fur China）摘录的译文：

一起新的军火案。

昨日的《字林西报》（The China Press）以类似大幅广告的风格，报道了在斐伦路（Ferry Road）查获一批弹药一事。警务处的调查结果显示，该行动完全合法，但《字林西报》却以一种相当无耻的方式将此事件与尼尔森案（Nielsens case）联系起来。
实际情况如下：
周六上午，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的一名英国巡警在巡逻时，注意到斐伦路码头有一艘由一名身穿海军制服的中国人负责的船只。当巡警对其进行询问时，他回答说正在等待装运至兵工厂的弹药。
巡警将情况电话报告给戈登路（Gordon Rd）巡捕房，随后一名巡官抵达。
几分钟后，一辆由小马牵引的马车驶来，后面跟着五名中国人，以及来自上海的H. Thomsen先生和来自天津的Fritz Sommers先生。Sommers先生与中国政府签有合同，并随身携带了必要的许可证。
应巡官要求，全体人员随后前往戈登路巡捕房，那里的中国人和弹药被扣留。几位德国绅士的所有抗议均无济于事。Sommers先生、Thomsen先生和那名中国官员随后去见上海公共租界工部局警务处处长Mc Euen先生，后者告知他们需要许可证。身为上海陌生人的Sommers先生从德国领事馆获得了一份许可证，该许可证也由资深领事（比利时总领事Siffert）签署，但警方仍拒绝释放该中国人及弹药。
今天上午，这些中国人被带至混合法庭，在英国陪审判员Brant Jones面前受审，应警方请求，案件延期至周五审理。
Musso先生代表中国政府出庭。
在《字林西报》大肆渲染之后，《字林报》（North China Daily News）刊登了一篇出人意料地温和的文章。
警方逮捕五名中国人并扣押弹药的行为是非法的，这违反了《土地章程》附律第87条，该条规定，如果由负责任的中国官员负责，通过国际租界运输武器和弹药无需许可证；在本案中，运输过程由一名中国海军军官陪同。
